summary: ALL THREE OF O15'S OPT FINDINGS ARE THE SAME ANSWER AND I CHECKED THE OTHER TWO ARMS BEFORE TAKING IT. THE ENDPOINT QUESTION WAS SETTLED FIRST, BY RUNNING, AND IT IS THE ONE THE BRIEF SAID was most likely to bite in opt: it does NOT bite on these three. `not 0.0 <= decay <= 1.0` excludes both 0.0 and 1.0 from what it refuses, `damp > 1.0` excludes 1.0, `damp < 0.0` excludes 0.0 -- so all three agree with a CLOSED [0.0, 1.0] at both ends exactly. Driven rather than read: 20 values per lever from -1e9 to 1e26 (including -0.0, -1e-09, 0.9999999999999999, 1.0, 1.0000000000000002, nan, inf, -inf), one fresh process each, through a real spine.assemble.build followed by a real OPT.build, with the pair in place and then NEUTRALISED in a scratch copy of the tree outside the repository so the clause answered alone: 40 of 40 cells IDENTICAL in verdict, both endpoints building under either layer, both floating-point neighbours refused under either. Nothing is left for the clauses, so the fork is real and the third possibility is refuted. I TOOK THE RETIRE ARM ON ALL THREE, PER LEVER AND NOT AS ONE ANSWER, and the discriminator is the one the brief states: each clause knew a property OF THE NUMBER -- a multiplier above 1.0 is not a damping, below 0.0 it flips the swing's sign, a convex blend weight outside [0,1] is not a blend -- and a (lo, hi) pair states exactly that. None knew a bound that depends on another lever, on an arm or on the mechanism. THE COUNTER-CASE IS IN THE SAME FUNCTION AND I LEFT IT ALONE: OPT_LR_MIN_FRAC's `not 0.0 <= min_frac < 1.0` refuses 1.0, which its own domain=(0.0, 1.0) ADMITS, so the two do not overlap and both are live -- O15 does not report it and it still fires by name (driven: OPT_LR_MIN_FRAC=1.0 -> ValueError from src/opt/api.py::build; 1.0000000000000002 -> LeverError from the pair). THE MEASUREMENT MOVED AND ONE SENTENCE OF IT WAS CORRECTED ON THE WAY: the damp>1.0 message said a value above 1.0 AMPLIFIES every failed restart, and src/opt/api.py::maybe_step guards its one `st.restart_amp *= ...` with `float(opt.lr_restart_damp) < 1.0`, so above 1.0 the loop goes INERT and amplifies nothing. That prose had rotted WHILE IT COULD STILL PRINT, which is the strongest argument in this report against keeping a measurement only inside a raise. It is now on the declaration, corrected and marked as corrected, beside the -1.0 / 2.0 curves already measured for lr_decay. WHAT THE OTHER EIGHT NOW DO, SAID PLAINLY BECAUSE THE BRIEF ASKED: nothing changed for them and nothing about OPT is now covered. Eight lever refusals remain in OPT.build -- seven one-sided comparisons (lr <= 0.0, weight_decay < 0.0, warmup < 0, wavelength < 0, accum < 1, batch_windows < 1, grad_clip < 0.0) and ONE inverted chain (min_frac), down from nine + two; all eighteen before/after cells over those eight are byte-identical. They are still range checks that do not bound the range: OPT_LR=1e30 builds on the edited tree, AdamW takes lr=1e+30, the horizon prints normally. THE TWELFTH REFUSAL STAYS AND NOW SAYS WHY: with REFUSE_NON_FINITE_FLOAT on it cannot fire from a lever at all, but that constant IS A SWITCH and with it off the twelfth is the only thing standing over OPT_LR, OPT_WEIGHT_DECAY and OPT_GRAD_CLIP (driven both arms). That is precisely the argument the three retired clauses did NOT have: domain= carries no switch by design, so a clause its pair covers is dead in every arm there is. THREE OF OPT'S SIX FLOATS NOW CARRY A PAIR AND THREE DO NOT, because lr, weight_decay and grad_clip have no derivable ceiling -- the condition 131 of the tree's 207 numeric levers are in. O15 no longer names any OPT lever; the suite is green everywhere except O15's two remaining findings, SIG_WARMUP_MIN_FRAC and TOK_DROPOUT, which belong to other owners.

findings.item: THE ENDPOINT TEST, RUN FIRST: all three read-site clauses and the closed pair [0.0, 1.0] agree EXACTLY at 0.0 and at 1.0, so the 'neither retire nor drop' answer does not apply to any of the three
findings.detail: The brief's third possibility is the one to disprove before touching anything, and it is disproved by running rather than by reading the operators. `not 0.0 <= decay <= 1.0` refuses (-inf, 0.0) U (1.0, inf) and ACCEPTS both ends; `damp > 1.0` accepts 1.0; `damp < 0.0` accepts 0.0. The declared domain is CLOSED at both ends, so it accepts both ends too. 40 cells (2 levers x 20 values) were driven with the pair in place and again with it neutralised in a scratch copy of the tree, one fresh process per cell, through a real spine.assemble.build and a real OPT.build: the accept/refuse verdict is the same in every cell. The only difference is WHICH layer refuses and WHAT it says. The live counter-example is in the same function and stays: OPT_LR_MIN_FRAC's chain is HALF-OPEN and refuses the 1.0 its pair admits.
findings.repro: SHIPPED (pair on): OPT_LR_DECAY=1.0 -> 'OPT.build OK | lr_decay=1.0 ...'; OPT_LR_DECAY=1.0000000000000002 -> 'REFUSED AT ASSEMBLE | LeverError raised in src/spine/lever.py:coerce | OPT_LR_DECAY=1.0000000000000002 is outside its declared domain [0.0, 1.0] -- BOTH ENDS INCLUSIVE'. Same pair of runs at the low end: -0.0 and 0.0 build under both; -1e-09 is refused under both. OPT_LR_RESTART_DAMP identical: 1.0 builds under both, 1.0000000000000002 refused under both ('is above 1.0' from the clause, 'outside its declared domain' from the pair); 0.0 and -0.0 build under both, -1e-09 refused under both ('is negative' / 'outside its declared domain'). CONTROL, shipped tree: OPT_LR_MIN_FRAC=1.0 -> 'REFUSED AT OPT.build | ValueError raised in src/opt/api.py:build | OPT_LR_MIN_FRAC=1.0 is outside [0.0, 1.0). It is a fraction of peak and 1.0 would make the cosine a constant.' -- the clause its pair leaves live, at exactly one point.

findings.item: OPT_LR_DECAY -- `not 0.0 <= decay <= 1.0` RETIRED from src/opt/api.py::build into the declaration's domain=(0.0, 1.0), with its measurement carried
findings.detail: Retired, not deleted. The pair refuses the same set one layer earlier, inside spine/lever.py::Lever.coerce, under the same generated env name, at the first read. Its message's content -- '0.0 restores the pre-2026-08-26 behaviour (restarts return to full peak) and 1.0 is the full envelope; the values between are meaningful and the ones outside are not' -- is now written on the declaration beside the pair, which already carried the stronger measurement: at decay=-1.0 the envelope is skipped entirely and the curve is step-for-step identical to decay=0.0, and at decay=2.0 the blend goes negative and 110 of 200 steps pin at lr_min_frac against 45 at the shipped 1.0. The reason the pair is the one that survived rather than the clause: what the clause knew is a property of the number (a convex blend weight outside [0,1] is not a blend), which is what a pair says; and the consumer re-reads the Config rather than this function's local -- src/opt/api.py::_priced takes `decay=float(opt.lr_decay)` off the frozen object -- so the declaration governs the value every reader sees while the local governed a copy.

findings.item: OPT_LR_RESTART_DAMP -- both `damp > 1.0` and `damp < 0.0` RETIRED into the declaration's domain=(0.0, 1.0)
findings.detail: Same ruling, weighed separately. `damp < 0.0` said 'a negative multiplier flips the sign of the restart swing', which is a property of the number and is the sentence the declaration comment already states from the arithmetic. `damp > 1.0` is the one that needed care: its bound is the identity multiplier, also a property of the number, and 1.0 is a SETTING (the identity at which no losing cycle can damp, which src/opt/api.py::counters prints as its own gate arm) so the closed end is right. Both clauses' arguments, including the old `min(1.0, max(0.0, ...))` clamp at :4739 they replaced, are now on the declaration.

findings.item: THE RETIRED damp>1.0 MESSAGE WAS FALSE WHEN IT WAS RETIRED, AND THE CORRECTED SENTENCE IS WHAT WENT ONTO THE DECLARATION
findings.detail: It said 'a value above 1.0 AMPLIFIES every failed restart instead of shrinking it'. src/opt/api.py::maybe_step guards its one `st.restart_amp *= float(opt.lr_restart_damp)` with `float(opt.lr_restart_damp) < 1.0`, so above 1.0 nothing is multiplied and the closed loop goes INERT. The declaration now records the refusal's reason (a number asking for the ratchet is not a damping) and, separately, what the mechanism would actually have done, marked as a correction so nobody requotes the old sentence. This is also the strongest argument in this report for the retire arm over the drop arm: prose inside a raise is not automatically better than prose beside a declaration -- this piece rotted while it could still print, and O15's own block had already caught it.
findings.repro: The false text is gone with the clause; `git diff src/opt/api.py` shows the removed lines 'multiplies the restart amplitude CUMULATIVELY, so a value above 1.0 AMPLIFIES every' and the docstring bullet that repeated it. src/opt/levers.py now carries 'THAT SENTENCE WAS ALREADY WRONG WHEN IT WAS RETIRED' with the guard quoted. Its old home is also the one site .rework/audits/d_lever.json listed as item (9) -- 'the only thing standing there and a Lever has no range facility.' inside a raised message -- which is now resolved by deletion rather than by edit.

findings.item: THE OTHER EIGHT REFUSALS ARE UNCHANGED, MEASURED CELL BY CELL, AND THE RETIREMENT IS NOT 'OPT IS NOW COVERED'
findings.detail: Eight lever refusals remain in OPT.build: seven one-sided comparisons (lr <= 0.0, weight_decay < 0.0, lr_warmup < 0, lr_wavelength < 0, accum < 1, batch_windows < 1, grad_clip < 0.0) and one inverted chain (lr_min_frac), plus the twelfth non-finite scan and the param_groups key refusal, which are not lever-range checks. WHAT THE EIGHT DO IS WHAT THEY DID: they are range checks that do not bound the range. OPT_LR=1e30 still builds on the edited tree and AdamW takes lr=1e+30. Three of OPT's six float levers carry a pair (lr_restart_damp, lr_decay, lr_min_frac -- each a ratio whose ends are readable off its own arithmetic) and three do not (lr, weight_decay, grad_clip), because no honest reading of those three declarations produces a ceiling.
